newsitem.title: USA: Chiron finds possible use for Herpes drug.
newsitem.headline: Chiron finds possible use for Herpes drug.

text.p: After a careful study of Phase III test results, Chiron Corp said Tuesday a vaccine it had been testing to fight Herpes Simplex Type 2 virus (HSV-2), may help ease symptoms of Herpes sufferers.
In January, the company said its vaccine did not reach the primary endpoints of a Phase III trials, and that it would continue to study results.

Today, at the Interscience Conference on Antimicrobial Agents and Chemotherapy (ICAAC) in New Orleans, Chiron told doctors the vaccine helped reduce the duration of outbreaks, the number of new skin lesions and the time for healing.

The test results give Chiron reason to possibly continue testing the vaccine, a spokesman said. He added, however, the company currently has two other trials in which Herpes vaccines are being tested.
"We really want to wait until we see the results of those preventive trials (before continuing)," the spokesman said.

In the trials, patients with frequently occurring genital herpes (7.0 outbreaks a year) received two doses of the vaccine or placebo at 0 and 2 months with detailed assessments of the first outbreak after the first immunization.

Immunization with the active vaccine was associated with a decrease in the duration of symptoms, from 6.7 to 4.9, a fall in the number of days on which new lesions formed, from 6.9 to 4.1 days, and healing time, from 8.8 to 6.8 days.
The recombinant vaccine was found to be generally well-tolerated, although some local and systemic reactions were seen in patients treated with vaccine.
